items.label: Include Script
items.content:
# Including the AIClient Library

To begin using AIClient in a browser environment, you must first load the library. This can be done באמצעות a CDN, which allows you to integrate the client without any build tooling or package installation.

## Usage

```html
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/HyperRushNet/hrn-ai/client/1.0.3.min.js"></script>
```

## How It Works

When this script is loaded:

- The `AIClient` class becomes globally available in the browser
- All client methods are accessible without importing modules
- The library initializes in a lightweight, stateless manner

## When to Use CDN

| Scenario | Recommended |
|----------|------------|
| Static websites | Yes |
| Prototypes and demos | Yes |
| Production (browser) | Yes |
| Node.js environments | No |

## Notes

- The CDN version is optimized for browser usage only
- No additional dependencies are required
- Ensure the script is loaded before attempting to instantiate the client

items.label: Initialize Client
items.content:
# Initializing the AIClient

After loading the library, the next step is to create a new client instance and configure authentication.

## Usage

```javascript
const client = new AIClient()
  .setApiKey('YOUR_API_KEY');
```

## Description

The API key is required for all interactions with the AI service. It is used to:

- Authenticate requests
- Track usage and enforce rate limits
- Determine access to specific models and features

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|----------|------|----------|-------------|
| apiKey | string | Yes | Unique API key issued to the user |

## Behavior

- The client stores the API key internally after initialization
- All subsequent requests automatically include this key
- If the key is missing or invalid, all requests will fail

## Security Considerations

- Do not expose your API key in publicly accessible client-side code in production
- Use environment variables or a proxy server for secure deployments

## Common Errors

| Error | Cause |
|------|------|
| Authentication failed | Invalid or missing API key |
| Unauthorized request | API key does not have required permissions |

items.label: Set Type to Text
items.content:
# Configuring Text Generation Mode

Before generating output, the client must be configured to operate in text mode. This determines how the input is interpreted and what type of response is returned.

## Usage

```javascript
client.setType('text');
```

## Description

Setting the type to `text` configures the client to:

- Accept string-based prompts
- Route requests to text-capable models
- Return responses as plain strings

## Supported Types

| Type | Input | Output |
|------|------|--------|
| text | string | string |
| image | string | Blob |

## Internal Behavior

- The client adjusts request formatting based on the selected type
- Validation rules differ depending on the type
- Incompatible settings (e.g. image dimensions in text mode) are ignored or may throw errors

## Important Notes

- This step is mandatory before calling `generate()`
- Changing the type resets certain internal configurations

items.label: Select Model
items.content:
# Selecting a Text Model

After configuring the client for text generation, you must select a model.

## Usage

```javascript
client.setModel('gemini-fast');
```

## Description

The model defines how the input prompt is processed and how the output is generated. Different models may vary in:

- Response speed
- Output quality
- Cost per request

## Available Models

| Model | Speed | Quality | Use Case |
|------|------|--------|----------|
| gemini-fast | High | Moderate | Real-time applications, chat interfaces |

## Behavior

- The selected model is applied to all subsequent requests
- Changing the model does not reset other configurations

## Considerations

- Use faster models for interactive applications
- Use higher-quality models (if available) for content generation tasks

## Errors

| Error | Cause |
|------|------|
| Model not found | Invalid model name |
| Unsupported model | Model not compatible with selected type |

items.label: Generate Text
items.content:
# Generating Text Output

Once the client is fully configured, you can generate text using the `generate()` method.

## Usage

```javascript
const result = await client.generate('Explain how AIClient works');
console.log(result);
```

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|----------|------|----------|-------------|
| prompt | string | Yes | Input text prompt |

## Return Value

| Type | Description |
|------|-------------|
| string | Generated text output |

## Execution Flow

1. Validate configuration (API key, type, model)
2. Send request to API
3. Wait for model response
4. Parse and return output

## Error Handling

| Error | Cause |
|------|------|
| Missing API key | Authentication not configured |
| Missing model | Model not set |
| Empty prompt | Invalid input |

## Best Practices

- Use clear and specific prompts
- Avoid extremely long inputs unless necessary
- Handle errors using try/catch

children.label: System Prompt
children.content:
# System Prompt

The system prompt provides high-level instructions that influence how the model responds.

## Usage

```javascript
client.setSystemPrompt('You are a technical assistant');
```

## Description

- Acts as a persistent instruction layer
- Applied to every request
- Useful for defining tone, role, or constraints

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required |
|----------|------|----------|
| prompt | string | No |

## Use Cases

- Enforcing consistent tone
- Restricting output format
- Defining assistant behavior

children.label: Timeout
children.content:
# Timeout Configuration

Defines the maximum time the client will wait for a response.

## Usage

```javascript
client.setTimeout(30000);
```

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default |
|----------|------|--------|
| timeout | number (ms) | 30000 |

## Behavior

- Requests exceeding this time are aborted
- Useful for preventing hanging requests

children.label: Seed
children.content:
# Seed

The seed ensures reproducibility of outputs.

## Usage

```javascript
client.setSeed(12345);
```

## Description

- Same seed + same input = similar output
- Primarily useful for testing and debugging

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default |
|----------|------|--------|
| seed | number | null |

children.label: Retry Logic
children.content:
# Retry Logic

Automatically retries failed requests.

## Usage

```javascript
client.setRetry(true, 2, 1000);
```

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| enabled | boolean | Enable or disable retry |
| attempts | number | Number of retry attempts |
| delay | number | Delay between retries (ms) |

## Behavior

- Retries only on failure
- Helps mitigate temporary network issues

items.label: Set Type to Image
items.content:
# Configuring Image Generation Mode

To generate images, the client must be switched to image mode.

## Usage

```javascript
client.setType('image');
```

## Description

This configuration:

- Enables image generation endpoints
- Changes the output format to binary (Blob)
- Activates image-specific validation rules

items.label: Select Model
items.content:
# Selecting an Image Model

## Usage

```javascript
client.setModel('flux');
```

## Description

The model determines how images are generated from prompts.

## Available Models

| Model | Description |
|------|------------|
| flux | General-purpose image generation |

## Considerations

- Model choice affects style and quality
- Some models may support additional parameters

items.label: Set Dimensions
items.content:
# Image Dimensions

Defines the output resolution of generated images.

## Usage

```javascript
client.setDimensions(1024, 1024);
```

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default |
|----------|------|--------|
| width | number | 1024 |
| height | number | 1024 |

## Behavior

- Larger dimensions increase detail
- Larger images require more processing time
- Some models may enforce limits
